title.raw: 卷一百四十六 志第九十九 儀衞四 Volume 146 Treatises 99: Ceremonial Guards 4

sentences.zh: 儀衛四○政和大駕鹵簿並宣和增減小駕附

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards 4: The Zhenghe Grand Imperial Escort, with Xuanhe-Era Additions and Reductions for the Minor Escort Attached
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards 4 — the Zhenghe grand imperial escort, with Xuanhe-era additions and reductions for the minor escort appended.

sentences.zh: 政和大駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe grand imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenghe grand imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 象六，分左右。

translations.literal: Six elephants, divided to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Six elephants, arrayed to the left and right.

sentences.zh: 次六引：開封令、開封牧、大司樂、少傅、御史大夫、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Next, the six leading contingents: the Prefect of Kaifeng, the Governor of Kaifeng, the Grand Director of Music, the Junior Mentor, the Censor-in-Chief, and the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the six leading contingents: the Prefect of Kaifeng, the Governor of Kaifeng, the Grand Director of Music, the Junior Mentor, the Censor-in-Chief, and the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 〈（各用本品鹵簿。）〉

translations.literal: (Each uses the escort appropriate to his rank.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each contingent employed the escort appropriate to its rank.)

sentences.zh: 次金吾纛、槊。

translations.literal: Next, the Jinwu banners and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Jinwu banners and spears.

sentences.zh: 左右皂纛各六，

translations.literal: Six black banners on the left and six on the right,
translations.idiomatic: Six black banners to the left and six to the right,

sentences.zh: 〈（執、托各一人，糸斥四人。）〉

translations.literal: (one bearer and one supporter each, and four pole handlers.)
translations.idiomatic: (one bearer and one supporter each, with four pole handlers.)

sentences.zh: 押衙四人，

translations.literal: four escort officers,
translations.idiomatic: four escort officers,

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 暴槊八，

translations.literal: eight ceremonial spears,
translations.idiomatic: eight ceremonial spears,

translations.literal: (one bearer each.)
translations.idiomatic: (one bearer each.)

sentences.zh: 本衛上將軍、將軍各四人，本衛大將軍二人，

translations.literal: four Senior Generals and four Generals of the guard each, and two Grand Generals of the guard,
translations.idiomatic: four Senior Generals and four Generals from the guard each, and two Grand Generals from the guard,

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 暴槊四，夾大將軍。

translations.literal: four ceremonial spears, flanking the Grand Generals.
translations.idiomatic: four ceremonial spears flanking the Grand Generals.

sentences.zh: 〈（執各一人，夾二人，並騎。）〉

translations.literal: (one bearer each; two flankers each; all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (one bearer each, two flankers each, all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 法駕，暴槊減二，本衛上將軍、將軍各減二人。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, two fewer ceremonial spears, and two fewer Senior Generals and Generals from the guard each.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were two fewer ceremonial spears and two fewer Senior Generals and Generals from the guard each.

sentences.zh: 次朱雀旗隊。

translations.literal: Next, the Vermilion Bird banner company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Vermilion Bird banner company.

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

translations.literal: One Breaker of Ranks colonel of the Jinwu Guard led the company; two ceremonial spears flanked the colonel;
translations.idiomatic: A Breaker of Ranks colonel of the Jinwu Guard led the company, with two ceremonial spears flanking him;

translations.literal: (one flag bearer; two leaders and two flankers each.

sentences.zh: 凡仗內引、夾、執人數準此。）〉

translations.literal: The numbers of leaders, flankers, and bearers within the honor guard follow this standard.)

sentences.zh: 弩四，弓矢十六，槊二十，左右金吾衛果毅都尉二人押隊。

translations.literal: four crossbows, sixteen bows with arrows, twenty spears, and two Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Jinwu Guards to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: four crossbows, sixteen bows with arrows, twenty spears, and two Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Jinwu Guards bringing up the rear.

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, two fewer crossbows, six fewer bows with arrows, and eight fewer spears.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were two fewer crossbows, six fewer bows with arrows, and eight fewer spears.

sentences.zh: 宣和，引隊改天武都指揮使，押隊改天武指揮使。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the company leader was changed to the Celestial Martial colonel-commander, and the rear guard to the Celestial Martial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the company leader was changed to the Celestial Martial colonel-commander and the rear guard to the Celestial Martial commander.

sentences.zh: 次龍旗隊。

translations.literal: Next, the Dragon banner company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Dragon banner company.

sentences.zh: 大將軍一員檢校，騎；

translations.literal: One Grand General served as inspector, mounted;
translations.idiomatic: One Grand General served as inspector, mounted;

sentences.zh: 引旗十二人，

translations.literal: twelve guidon bearers,
translations.idiomatic: twelve guidon bearers,

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 風伯、雨師、雷公、電母旗各一，五星旗五，左、右攝提旗二，北斗旗一，護旗十二人，副竿二。

translations.literal: one banner each for the Wind Lord, Rain Master, Thunder Duke, and Lightning Mother; five Five-Star banners; two banners each for the Left and Right Saddled Ladle; one Northern Dipper banner; twelve guard banners; and two secondary poles.
translations.idiomatic: one banner each for the Wind Lord, Rain Master, Thunder Duke, and Lightning Mother; five Five-Star banners; two Left and Right Saddled Ladle banners; one Northern Dipper banner; twelve guard banners; and two secondary poles.

sentences.zh: 〈（執人並騎。）〉

translations.literal: (all bearers mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all bearers mounted.)

sentences.zh: 法駕，引旗、護旗人各減四。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, four fewer guidon bearers and four fewer guard banners each.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were four fewer guidon bearers and four fewer guard banners each.

sentences.zh: 宣和，檢校改左右衛大將軍，雷公、電母旗去“公”、“母”二字。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the inspector was changed to Left and Right Guard Grand Generals, and the characters "duke" and "mother" were dropped from the Thunder Duke and Lightning Mother banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the inspector was changed to Left and Right Guard Grand Generals, and the characters for "duke" and "mother" were removed from the Thunder Duke and Lightning Mother banners.

sentences.zh: 次指南、記裏鼓車各一，駕馬各四，駕士各三十人，白鷺、鸞旗、崇德、皮軒車各一，駕士各十八人。

translations.literal: Next, one south-pointing chariot and one clepsydra drum chariot each, with four draft horses each and thirty drivers each; one White Egret chariot, one Simurgh banner chariot, one Exalted Virtue chariot, and one leather-canopy chariot each, with eighteen drivers each.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one south-pointing chariot and one clepsydra drum chariot, each with four draft horses and thirty drivers; and one White Egret chariot, one Simurgh banner chariot, one Exalted Virtue chariot, and one leather-canopy chariot, each with eighteen drivers.

sentences.zh: 法駕，無白鷺、崇德車。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, no White Egret or Exalted Virtue chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were no White Egret or Exalted Virtue chariots.

sentences.zh: 宣和，有青旌、青雀、鳴鳶、飛鴻、虎皮、貔貅六車，在記裏鼓之下、崇德之前；

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, six chariots were added—the Azure Pennant, Azure Sparrow, Singing Kite, Flying Wild Goose, Tiger Skin, and Pixiu chariots—placed below the clepsydra drum chariot and before the Exalted Virtue chariot;
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, six chariots were added—the Azure Pennant, Azure Sparrow, Singing Kite, Flying Wild Goose, Tiger Skin, and Pixiu chariots—placed below the clepsydra drum chariot and before the Exalted Virtue chariot;

sentences.zh: 減白鷺、鸞旗、皮軒三車，駕士之數如前。

translations.literal: three chariots were removed—the White Egret, Simurgh banner, and leather-canopy chariots—with the number of drivers as before.
translations.idiomatic: three chariots were removed—the White Egret, Simurgh banner, and leather-canopy chariots—with the number of drivers unchanged.

sentences.zh: 次金吾引駕，騎；

translations.literal: Next, the Jinwu escort leading the procession, mounted;
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Jinwu escort leading the procession, all mounted;

sentences.zh: 本衛果毅都尉二人，儀刀、弩、弓矢、槊各減二。

translations.literal: two Fruitful and Resolute colonels from the guard, with two fewer ceremonial swords, crossbows, bows with arrows, and spears each.
translations.idiomatic: two Fruitful and Resolute colonels from the guard, with two fewer ceremonial swords, crossbows, bows with arrows, and spears each.

sentences.zh: 宣和，改都尉為神勇都指揮使。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the colonels were changed to Divine Valor colonel-commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the colonels were changed to Divine Valor colonel-commanders.

sentences.zh: 次大晟府前部鼓吹。

translations.literal: Next, the front percussion ensemble of the Great Splendor Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the front percussion ensemble of the Great Splendor Bureau.

sentences.zh: 令二人，府史四人，管押指揮使一人，鞞鼓、金鉦各十二，

translations.literal: two Directors, four bureau clerks, one supervising colonel-commander, twelve hand drums and twelve metal gongs each,
translations.idiomatic: two Directors, four bureau clerks, one supervising colonel-commander, and twelve hand drums and twelve metal gongs each,

translations.idiomatic: (led by eight commanding officers.)

translations.idiomatic: one hundred and twenty great drums,

translations.literal: (led by twenty commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by twenty commanding officers.)

translations.literal: one hundred and twenty long trumpets,
translations.idiomatic: one hundred and twenty long trumpets,

translations.literal: (led by six commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by six commanding officers.)

sentences.zh: 鐃鼓十二，

translations.literal: twelve nao drums,
translations.idiomatic: twelve nao drums,

translations.literal: (led by four commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by four commanding officers.)

translations.literal: twenty-four singers, twenty-four Arched Canopy pipes, twenty-four vertical flutes, and twenty-four horns each; one hundred and twenty large horizontal pipes,
translations.idiomatic: twenty-four singers, twenty-four Arched Canopy pipes, twenty-four vertical flutes, and twenty-four horns each; one hundred and twenty large horizontal pipes,

translations.literal: (led by ten commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by ten commanding officers.)

translations.literal: two beat drums; twenty-four flutes, vertical flutes, bili pipes, horns, and peach-skin bili pipes each;
translations.idiomatic: two beat drums; twenty-four flutes, vertical flutes, bili pipes, horns, and peach-skin bili pipes each;

sentences.zh: 鞞鼓、金鉦各十二，

translations.literal: twelve hand drums and twelve metal gongs each,
translations.idiomatic: twelve hand drums and twelve metal gongs each,

sentences.zh: 〈（帥兵官四人領。）〉

translations.literal: (led by four commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by four commanding officers.)

sentences.zh: 小鼓、中鳴各一百二十，

translations.literal: one hundred and twenty small drums and one hundred and twenty mid trumpets each,
translations.idiomatic: one hundred and twenty small drums and one hundred and twenty mid trumpets each,

sentences.zh: 〈（帥兵官八人領。）〉

translations.literal: (led by eight commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by eight commanding officers.)

sentences.zh: 羽葆鼓十二，

translations.literal: twelve feathered canopy drums,
translations.idiomatic: twelve feathered canopy drums,

sentences.zh: 〈（帥兵官四人領。）〉

translations.literal: (led by four commanding officers.)
translations.idiomatic: (led by four commanding officers.)

translations.literal: twenty-four singers, twenty-four Arched Canopy pipes, twenty-four vertical flutes, and twenty-four horns each.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-four singers, twenty-four Arched Canopy pipes, twenty-four vertical flutes, and twenty-four horns each.

sentences.zh: 法駕，前後鞞鼓、金鉦各減四，大鼓減四十，長鳴減四十，鐃鼓減四，拱宸管後簫、笳各減八，大橫吹減四十，節鼓後笛、簫、觱篥、笳、桃皮觱篥各減八，小鼓、中鳴各減四十，羽葆鼓減四，最後簫、笳各減八，帥兵共減十八人。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, four fewer hand drums and metal gongs before and after; forty fewer great drums; forty fewer long trumpets; four fewer nao drums; eight fewer vertical flutes and horns after the Arched Canopy pipes; forty fewer large horizontal pipes; eight fewer flutes, vertical flutes, bili pipes, horns, and peach-skin bili pipes after the beat drums; forty fewer small drums and mid trumpets each; four fewer feathered canopy drums; eight fewer vertical flutes and horns at the end; eighteen fewer commanding officers in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were four fewer hand drums and metal gongs fore and aft; forty fewer great drums; forty fewer long trumpets; four fewer nao drums; eight fewer vertical flutes and horns after the Arched Canopy pipes; forty fewer large horizontal pipes; eight fewer flutes, vertical flutes, bili pipes, horns, and peach-skin bili pipes after the beat drums; forty fewer small drums and mid trumpets each; four fewer feathered canopy drums; eight fewer vertical flutes and horns at the end; and eighteen fewer commanding officers in all.

sentences.zh: 次太史相風、行漏等輿。

translations.literal: Next, the Directorate of Astronomy wind-vane and traveling clepsydra carriages and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Directorate of Astronomy wind-vane and traveling clepsydra carriages and the like.

sentences.zh: 太史令及令史各一人，

translations.literal: one Director of Astronomy and one clerk each,
translations.idiomatic: the Director of Astronomy and one clerk each,

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 相風烏輿一。

translations.literal: one wind-vane bird carriage.
translations.idiomatic: one wind-vane bird carriage.

sentences.zh: 〈（輿士四人。）〉

translations.literal: (four carriage attendants.)
translations.idiomatic: (four carriage attendants.)

sentences.zh: 交龍鉦、鼓各一，

translations.literal: one interlaced-dragon gong and one drum each,
translations.idiomatic: one interlaced-dragon gong and one drum each,

sentences.zh: 〈（輿士各六人。）〉

translations.literal: (six carriage attendants each.)
translations.idiomatic: (six carriage attendants each.)

sentences.zh: 司辰、典士各一人，

translations.literal: one timekeeper and one master of ceremonies each,
translations.idiomatic: one timekeeper and one master of ceremonies each,

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

sentences.zh: 漏刻生四人，鼓樓、鍾樓、行漏輿各一，

translations.literal: four clepsydra students; one drum tower carriage, one bell tower carriage, and one traveling clepsydra carriage each,
translations.idiomatic: four clepsydra students; one drum tower carriage, one bell tower carriage, and one traveling clepsydra carriage each,

translations.literal: (one hundred carriage attendants each.)
translations.idiomatic: (one hundred carriage attendants each.)

translations.literal: one Chief Astronomer, two path-clearers, and one Twelve Spirits carriage.
translations.idiomatic: one Chief Astronomer, two path-clearers, and one Twelve Spirits carriage.

sentences.zh: 〈（輿士十四人。）〉

translations.literal: (fourteen carriage attendants.)
translations.idiomatic: (fourteen carriage attendants.)

sentences.zh: 法駕，行漏輿一，

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, one traveling clepsydra carriage,
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there was one traveling clepsydra carriage,

sentences.zh: 〈（輿士減四十人。）〉

translations.literal: (forty fewer carriage attendants.)
translations.idiomatic: (with forty fewer carriage attendants.)

sentences.zh: 神輿一，

translations.literal: one Spirits carriage,
translations.idiomatic: one Spirits carriage,

sentences.zh: 〈（輿士多大駕二人。）〉

translations.literal: (with two more carriage attendants than in the grand escort.)
translations.idiomatic: (with two more carriage attendants than in the grand escort.)

sentences.zh: 宣和，鼓、鍾樓並改為輿，太史正前有捧日副指揮使二人，捧日節級十人，神輿輿士增十。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the drum and bell towers were both changed to carriages; before the Chief Astronomer were two vice commanders of the Sun-Upholders, ten Sun-Upholder rankers, and ten additional carriage attendants for the Spirits carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the drum and bell towers were both changed to carriages; before the Chief Astronomer stood two vice commanders of the Sun-Upholders and ten Sun-Upholder rankers, and ten carriage attendants were added to the Spirits carriage.

sentences.zh: 次持鈒前隊。

translations.literal: Next, the front company bearing ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the front company bearing ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 左右武衛果毅都尉二人引隊，左右武衛校尉二人。

translations.literal: Two Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Martial Guards led the company; two Captains of the Left and Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Two Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Martial Guards led the company, with two Captains of the Left and Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 絳引幡一，

translations.literal: one crimson guidon banner,
translations.idiomatic: one crimson guidon banner,

sentences.zh: 〈（糸斥二人。）〉

translations.literal: (two pole handlers.)
translations.idiomatic: (two pole handlers.)

sentences.zh: 左右有金節十二，

translations.literal: twelve golden regalia-staffs to left and right,
translations.idiomatic: twelve golden regalia-staffs to the left and right,

sentences.zh: 〈（執人並騎。）〉

translations.literal: (all bearers mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all bearers mounted.)

sentences.zh: 罕、罼各一，朱雀幢、叉、導蓋，青龍、白虎幢各一，叉三。

translations.literal: one each of the rare-game and net banners; one Vermilion Bird pennant, forks, and canopy guide; one Azure Dragon and one White Tiger pennant each; three forks.
translations.idiomatic: one rare-game banner and one net banner each; one Vermilion Bird pennant with forks and canopy guide; one Azure Dragon pennant and one White Tiger pennant; and three forks.

sentences.zh: 〈（執人並騎。）〉

translations.literal: (all bearers mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all bearers mounted.)

translations.literal: one herald chief; two hundred eighty-eight ceremonial halberds; two Generals of the Left and Right Martial Guards as inspectors; four Captains of the Left and Right Martial Guards to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: one herald chief; two hundred eighty-eight ceremonial halberds; two Generals of the Left and Right Martial Guards serving as inspectors; and four Captains of the Left and Right Martial Guards bringing up the rear.

sentences.zh: 法駕，金節減四，鈒戟減七十二。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, four fewer golden regalia-staffs and seventy-two fewer ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were four fewer golden regalia-staffs and seventy-two fewer ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 宣和，引隊改驍騎都指揮使，武衛校尉改驍騎軍使，增朱雀旗後之叉一，去龍虎旗後之叉三，檢校改用左右驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the company leader was changed to the Valiant Cavalry colonel-commander; Martial Guard captains to Valiant Cavalry army commissioners; one fork added after the Vermilion Bird banner; three forks removed after the dragon and tiger banners; inspectors changed to Left and Right Valiant Cavalry generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the company leader was changed to the Valiant Cavalry colonel-commander, Martial Guard captains to Valiant Cavalry army commissioners, one fork added after the Vermilion Bird banner, three forks removed after the dragon and tiger banners, and inspectors changed to Left and Right Valiant Cavalry generals.

translations.idiomatic: Next came one yellow command-banner.

translations.idiomatic: two pole handlers.)

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, two Palace Attendant censors were placed before it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, two Palace Attendant censors were placed before it.

translations.literal: Next, the Six Armies honor guard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Six Armies honor guard.

sentences.zh: 左右神武軍、左右羽林軍、左右龍武軍，各有統軍二員，都頭二人

translations.literal: Next, the court-sword and ceremonial-sword company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the court-sword and ceremonial-sword company.

sentences.zh: 並騎。

translations.literal: all mounted.
translations.idiomatic: all mounted.

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍二人分領，郎將二十四人，左右親衛、勳衛各四人，每衛班劍二百二十人；

translations.literal: Two Generals of the Left and Right Guard divided command; twenty-four Gentlemen; four each from the Left and Right Close Guard and Meritorious Guard; two hundred twenty court swords per guard;
translations.idiomatic: Two Generals of the Left and Right Guard divided command, with twenty-four Gentlemen, four each from the Left and Right Close Guard and Meritorious Guard, and two hundred twenty court swords per guard;

sentences.zh: 諸翊衛左右衛六人，領儀刀四百八人；

translations.literal: six Assist Guards of the Left and Right Guard, leading four hundred eight ceremonial swords;
translations.idiomatic: six Assist Guards of the Left and Right Guard leading four hundred eight ceremonial swords;

sentences.zh: 左右驍衛二人，領儀刀一百三十六人。

translations.literal: two from the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, leading one hundred thirty-six ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: two from the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry leading one hundred thirty-six ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 左右武衛、左右威衛、左右領軍衛、左右金吾衛各二人。

translations.idiomatic: Two each from the Left and Right Martial, Martial Display, Army Auspices, and Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 法駕，親、勳衛班劍減八十四人，翊衛儀刀減一百三十二人，增左右驍衛四人，班劍、儀刀九十二人。

sentences.zh: 宣和，分領改左右武衛將軍及捧日、天武指揮四人，拱聖六人，神勇、驍騎、驍勝、宣武、虎翼指揮使各二人。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, division of command was changed to Left and Right Martial generals and four commanders of Sun-Upholder and Celestial Martial; six of Arch-Sacred; and two colonel-commanders each of Divine Valor, Valiant Cavalry, Valiant Victory, Martial Display, and Tiger Wing.

sentences.zh: 次親勳、散手、驍衛翊衛隊。

translations.literal: Next, the Close-Meritorious, Free-Hand, and Valiant Cavalry Assist Guard companies.

translations.literal: (all mounted.)
translations.idiomatic: (all mounted.)

translations.literal: Four Palace Attendant Gentlemen of the Left and Right Guard divided command of forty-eight Close-Meritorious Assist Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Four Palace Attendant Gentlemen of the Left and Right Guard divided command of forty-eight Close-Meritorious Assist Guards;

sentences.zh: 左右衛郎將二人，分領散手翊衛六十人；

translations.literal: two Gentlemen of the Left and Right Guard divided command of sixty Free-Hand Assist Guards;
translations.idiomatic: two Gentlemen of the Left and Right Guard divided command of sixty Free-Hand Assist Guards;

sentences.zh: 法駕，親勳減十六人，散手、驍衛各減二十人。

translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were sixteen fewer Close-Meritorious guards and twenty fewer each for Free-Hand and Valiant Cavalry.

translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, they were changed to Central Guard, Assist Guard, and Close Guard companies; four Central Guard Gentlemen divided command of forty-eight guards;

translations.literal: two Assist Guard Gentlemen divided command of sixty guards;
translations.idiomatic: two Assist Guard Gentlemen divided command of sixty guards;

translations.literal: two Close Guard Gentlemen divided command of fifty-six guards.
translations.idiomatic: two Close Guard Gentlemen divided command of fifty-six guards.

sentences.zh: 次左右驍衛翊衛三隊。

translations.literal: Next, the three Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Assist Guard companies.

translations.literal: (all mounted.)

translations.literal: each had two men dividing command: the first, the home guard Grand General; the second, the home guard General; the third, the home guard Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: each had two men dividing command: the first by the home guard Grand General, the second by the home guard General, the third by the home guard Gentleman;

sentences.zh: 花鳳、飛黃、吉利旗各二，分為三隊；

translations.literal: two banners each for Flowery Phoenix, Flying Yellow, and Auspicious Profit, divided into three companies;
translations.idiomatic: two banners each for Flowery Phoenix, Flying Yellow, and Auspicious Profit, divided into three companies;

sentences.zh: 逐隊弩十，弓矢二十，槊四十。

translations.literal: each company had ten crossbows, twenty bows with arrows, and forty spears.
translations.idiomatic: each company had ten crossbows, twenty bows with arrows, and forty spears.

sentences.zh: 法駕，弩減四，弓矢、槊各減半。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, four fewer crossbows; bows with arrows and spears each reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were four fewer crossbows, and bows with arrows and spears were each reduced by half.

sentences.zh: 宣和，分領第一、第二隊，左右驍衛大將軍、將軍；

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, the first and second companies were led by Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Grand Generals and Generals;
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, the first and second companies were led by Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Grand Generals and Generals;

translations.literal: the third by the Broad Valor colonel-commander.
translations.idiomatic: the third by the Broad Valor colonel-commander.

translations.idiomatic: The Flowery Phoenix banner was changed to the Twin Lotus banner.

sentences.zh: 次來轂隊。

translations.literal: Next, the Coming Hub company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Coming Hub company.

sentences.zh: 凡六，逐隊都尉二人檢校，第一、第四左右衛折衝，第二、第三、第五、第六並左右衛果毅。

translations.literal: There were six in all; each company had two colonels as inspectors: the first and fourth, Breaker of Ranks colonels of the Left and Right Guard; the second, third, fifth, and sixth, Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: There were six in all; each company had two colonels as inspectors: the first and fourth by Breaker of Ranks colonels of the Left and Right Guard, and the second, third, fifth, and sixth by Fruitful and Resolute colonels of the Left and Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 逐隊刀盾各六十人，內第一、第四有寶符旗二。

translations.literal: Each company had sixty sword-shields; within the first and fourth were two Treasure Talisman banners.
translations.idiomatic: Each company had sixty sword-shields; within the first and fourth were two Treasure Talisman banners.

sentences.zh: 法駕，各減刀盾二十。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, twenty fewer sword-shields each.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, there were twenty fewer sword-shields each.

sentences.zh: 宣和，檢校改為捧日、天武、拱聖三指揮使。

translations.literal: Under Xuanhe, inspectors were changed to Sun-Upholder, Celestial Martial, and Arch-Sacred colonel-commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe period, inspectors were changed to Sun-Upholder, Celestial Martial, and Arch-Sacred colonel-commanders.

sentences.zh: 次捧日隊。

translations.literal: Next, the Sun-Upholder company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Sun-Upholder company.

translations.literal: Each company had one leader, two rear guards, twenty-eight long-running hall attendants, three banner heads, five spearmen, twenty archers, and one hundred fifty-five Celestial Martial interceptors in each wing.
translations.idiomatic: Each company had one leader, two rear guards, twenty-eight long-running hall attendants, three banner heads, five spearmen, twenty archers, and one hundred fifty-five Celestial Martial interceptors in each wing.

sentences.zh: 法駕，同。

sentences.zh: 次後部黃麾仗。

translations.literal: Next, the rear yellow command guard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the rear yellow command guard.

sentences.zh: 分六部：左右衛、左右驍衛、左右武衛、左右威衛、左右領軍衛、左右武衛。

translations.literal: Divided into six sections: Left and Right Guard, Valiant Cavalry, Martial, Martial Display, Army Auspices, and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: It was divided into six sections: Left and Right Guard, Valiant Cavalry, Martial, Martial Display, Army Auspices, and Martial.

sentences.zh: 部內殿中侍御史、大將軍、都尉、帥兵官、絳引幡、龍頭竿等，並同前部。

translations.literal: Within each section, Palace Attendant censors, Grand Generals, colonels, commanding officers, crimson guidon banners, dragon-head poles, and the like were all the same as in the front section.
translations.idiomatic: Within each section, Palace Attendant censors, Grand Generals, colonels, commanding officers, crimson guidon banners, dragon-head poles, and the like were all the same as in the front section.

sentences.zh: 法駕，減第六部，絳引幡減六。

translations.literal: For the statutory escort, the sixth section was removed and six crimson guidon banners were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutory escort, the sixth section was removed and six crimson guidon banners were removed.

sentences.zh: 宣和，六部：第一改為左右驍衛大將軍，自二至六改為天武、神勇、宣武、虎翼、廣勇五指揮。

translations.idiomatic: Next came the rear foot-armor companies.

translations.literal: There were twelve in all, each with two colonels dividing command.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve in all, each with two colonels dividing command.

translations.literal: The first led by the Left and Right Guard; the third by the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry; the fifth by the Left and Right Martial; the seventh by the Left and Right Martial Display; the ninth and eleventh each by the Left and Right Army Auspices — all Fruitful and Resolute;
translations.idiomatic: The first was led by the Left and Right Guard, the third by the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, the fifth by the Left and Right Martial, the seventh by the Left and Right Martial Display, and the ninth and eleventh each by the Left and Right Army Auspices — all Fruitful and Resolute;

translations.idiomatic: Each company had bows with arrows and sword-shields alternating, sixty men each, placed behind the banners.

translations.idiomatic: Next came the rear horse companies.

translations.literal: There were twelve in all, each led by two colonels.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve in all, each led by two colonels.

translations.literal: the third and fourth each by the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry; the eighth and ninth by the Left and Right Martial Display — all Fruitful and Resolute.

translations.literal: four fewer crossbows; six fewer bows with arrows; twelve fewer spears.
translations.idiomatic: there were four fewer crossbows, six fewer bows with arrows, and twelve fewer spears.
